assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a value with the same variable the test passed in: WAIVER_REASON travels through the completion's waiver record and the manifest before the row is read, and the counted case compares the row against a literal written in the test. Two added lines (396, 397) assert only the absence of traceback wording and name no positive control in its place.

findings.text: the uncounted branch drops a present integer failure_count whenever completed is not True, so a well-formed arm carrying completed false and a real count is recorded as no-count and its count is lost; both production callers pre-validate through suite_observation_missing_fields so it is unreachable today, but the helper is public and now accepts a shape wider than it preserves

suite_observation_is_uncounted restates the counted-or-not rule that suite_observation_missing_fields already owns, and the two disagree — a negative or bool failure_count is missing there and counted here — so the refusal clause driven by this predicate can drift from the validation that admitted the arm
_revisions is defined and never called — the module calls _revisions_head and its own git rev-parse instead — leaving a dead helper in a newly added test module
